analysis.title: BofA Securities Equity Client Flow Trends: More TMT selling but big Utilities inflows
key_insights: Clients sold US equities last week (S&P 500 +2.5%) after buying the prior week. Single stocks saw -$3.3bn of outflows, the 5th straight week of outflows. Equity ETFs saw $1.5bn of inflows, the 5th straight week.

Retail (private) clients drove the selling and have sold for 5 weeks. The 4-week average of their net flows is the lowest since April 2025. Hedge funds also sold equities, while institutional clients bought for the 2nd straight week.
By size segment, only mid cap equities saw inflows last week. Large cap equities (stocks + ETFs) saw -$2.24bn, with large cap single stocks at -$3.65bn.

Corporate client buybacks decelerated for the 2nd straight week. Annualized YTD buybacks are tracking below 2024-25 levels but above 2010-23 annual levels. Rolling 52-week buybacks as a % of S&P 500 market cap are 0.18%, the lowest since 2021.
Clients sold stocks in 7 of 11 sectors, led by Tech (-$1.87bn single stocks) and Comm. Svcs. (-$1.01bn). Both have seen outflows most weeks since mid-October.
Clients sold Energy stocks for the 2nd week as oil fell. They sold both Consumer sectors, with the first Cons. Disc. outflows in 6 weeks.

Utilities saw the 2nd largest inflows ever (7th largest normalized by market cap), at +$811mn single stocks, despite higher rates and continued AI-related worries. Utilities has had 3 weeks of inflows after consistent outflows since mid-September.
In the prior 6 times Utilities inflows/market cap were this large, Utilities outperformed over the subsequent 4 weeks in all but one instance, by an average of 2ppt.
Industrials saw inflows for the 1st time in 16 weeks, after its longest outflow streak since Jan 2024.
ETF flows split from single stock flows: first Value ETF outflows since July, with Blend/Growth ETFs bought and large/broad market cap ETFs bought versus mid/small cap ETFs sold.
ETF outflows hit 7 of 11 sectors, led by Real Estate, while Tech ETFs saw the biggest inflows (+$338mn), the opposite of single stock flows.
Hedge fund single stock flows were -$1.1bn last week, the 5th straight week of 4-week average outflows. Institutional 4-week average single stock flows turned positive for the first time in 8 weeks.
Year to date, clients have net sold $108.9bn of single stocks and bought $72.3bn of equity ETFs. Total stocks plus ETFs is -$36.6bn.
Hedge funds are net buyers of single stocks YTD (+$13.1bn), while institutional (-$60.6bn) and private clients (-$61.4bn) are net sellers.

sector_views.rationale: Flows are near record at +$811mn single stocks last week, and past episodes of similarly large inflows were followed by 4-week outperformance in 5 of 6 cases. This is a flow observation and not an explicit rating.

Client single stock outflows of -$1.87bn last week, with 4-week average outflows for the 7th week. Tech ETFs saw inflows, so the stock selling is not mirrored in ETFs. This is a flow observation and not an explicit rating.
Single stock outflows of -$1.01bn last week and 4-week average outflows for the 5th straight week. This is a flow observation and not an explicit rating.

risk_factors: Continued AI-related worries and a tick back up in rates are noted as backdrop for Utilities flows.
Retail and hedge fund selling, along with weak corporate buybacks, may reduce support for the market after a +2.5% week.
Weekly flow data can be influenced by block trades and is more volatile than the 4-week average.
charts_described: Exhibit 3 plots weekly Utilities net flows normalized by S&P 500 Utilities market cap since 2008. BofA's caption says it is the largest inflow since Sept. 2024 on that basis.
Exhibit 21 plots rolling 52-week corporate client buybacks as a % of S&P 500 market cap. BofA's caption says it peaked at 0.42% in Feb. 2025 and is at 0.18%, the lowest since 2021.
vol_and_positioning: Retail clients have sold for 5 straight weeks. The 4-week average of their net flows is the lowest since April 2025.
Hedge fund 4-week average single stock outflows have run 5 straight weeks, and equity (stock + ETF) outflows 3 straight weeks.
Large cap 4-week average single stock and total equity outflows have run 8 straight weeks.
Utilities flows normalized by sector market cap are the largest since September 2024. Utilities z-scores last week were 1.93 (3m), 2.53 (1y) and 3.70 (5y).
Industrials z-scores last week were 1.97 (3m), 1.00 (1y) and 1.27 (5y), as the sector had its first inflows in 16 weeks.
Growth ETF 1-year z-scores of 2.67 and Tech ETF 1-year z-scores of 2.51 show strong ETF demand for growth and tech over the past year.
